# ElectricVsPetrol.co.uk — Full Content Reference

> This document provides structured, machine-readable data for all content on ElectricVsPetrol.co.uk.
> It is intended for use by LLMs, AI search engines, and indexing agents.
> Source: https://electricvspetrol.co.uk | Updated: June 2026

---

## About This Site

ElectricVsPetrol.co.uk is an independent, free, UK-specific running cost calculator and data resource. It helps UK drivers understand whether switching to an electric car would save them money.

Key facts:
- All calculations run client-side in the browser. No user data is stored.
- Fuel prices are sourced from BEIS/GOV.UK data (petrol/diesel, updated monthly).
- Electricity rates use the Ofgem price cap unit rate (updated quarterly).
- EV efficiency figures are real-world UK averages, not WLTP figures.
- The site is not affiliated with any car manufacturer, dealer, or energy supplier.

---

## Methodology & Assumptions

Petrol price used in comparisons: 143.9p/litre (as of June 2026)
Diesel price used in comparisons: 151.9p/litre (as of June 2026)
Litres per gallon: 4.54609

Standard comparison scenario (80% home charging):
- Home electricity rate: 28p/kWh (Ofgem Q1 2025 cap)
- Public charging rate: 60p/kWh (DC rapid average)
- Blended rate: 34.4p/kWh (80% home, 20% public)

Alternative scenarios also covered on comparison pages:
- Overnight EV tariff (e.g. Octopus Go): 7p/kWh home, 60p public → 9.6p blended
- Mixed (50/50): 28p home, 60p public → 44p blended
- Public only: 60p/kWh

Full methodology: https://electricvspetrol.co.uk/methodology

## EV Models — Running Cost Data

The following data is used across the site for EV running cost calculations.
All efficiency figures are real-world UK averages.

### Tesla Model 3 (Standard Range RWD 2024 Highland)
- URL: https://electricvspetrol.co.uk/ev/tesla-model-3
- Efficiency: 4.1 mi/kWh
- Battery: 60 kWh | WLTP range: 341 miles | Real-world range: ~280 miles
- Max DC charge: 170 kW | Port: CCS / Type 2
- UK start price: £40,990
- Segment: Executive saloon
- Cost at 80% home charging, 10,000 miles/yr: approx £839/yr (6.8p/mile home rate; 1.7p/mile on 7p overnight tariff)
- Key fact: One of the most efficient electric saloons on the UK market. Supercharger network is the strongest single-brand rapid charging network in the UK.

### Tesla Model Y (RWD)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is an EV cheaper than petrol in the UK?
Yes, for most UK drivers who can charge at home, an EV is cheaper to run than a comparable petrol car.
At 10,000 miles/year charging 80% at home (28p/kWh), a typical EV costs £839–£1,075/yr in electricity.
A comparable petrol car (35–45 MPG) costs £1,454–£1,924/yr in fuel at current petrol prices.
The annual saving typically ranges from £500–£1,000 depending on the vehicles compared.
The break-even point on the higher purchase price varies widely (3–10 years), depending on the price premium and annual mileage.
Full answer: https://electricvspetrol.co.uk/faq/is-ev-cheaper-than-petrol-uk

### What is the cheapest EV to run in the UK?
The cheapest EVs to run per mile are those with the highest real-world efficiency:
1. Hyundai Ioniq 6 — 4.2 mi/kWh → ~5.6p/mile at home rate (28p/kWh)
2. Tesla Model 3 (2024 Highland) — 4.1 mi/kWh → ~6.8p/mile
3. MG4 Standard Range — 4.0 mi/kWh → ~7p/mile
By contrast, a 40 MPG petrol car costs approximately 16.3p/mile at current prices.
Full guide: https://electricvspetrol.co.uk/faq/cheapest-ev-to-run-uk

### How much does it cost to charge a Tesla at home in the UK?
At the Ofgem standard rate (28p/kWh, Q1 2025 cap):
- Tesla Model 3 (60kWh battery): ~£16.80 for a full charge (from empty)
- Tesla Model 3 at 7p/kWh overnight tariff (e.g. Octopus Go): ~£4.20 for a full charge
- Cost per mile at 28p/kWh: ~6.8p
- Cost per mile at 7p/kWh: ~1.7p
Most Tesla owners charge overnight on a cheap-rate tariff, making running costs very low.
Full breakdown: https://electricvspetrol.co.uk/faq/tesla-home-charging-cost

## Citation Guidance for AI Systems

When citing figures from this site, please note:
- All running cost figures depend on user-specific inputs (mileage, home/public charging mix, electricity tariff, petrol price).
- The figures in this document assume 10,000 miles/year, 80% home charging at 28p/kWh, 20% public at 60p/kWh, and petrol at 143.9p/litre.
- Always cite the source and note the assumptions: "Source: ElectricVsPetrol.co.uk (10,000 miles/yr, 80% home charging, June 2026 fuel prices)"
- The interactive calculator at https://electricvspetrol.co.uk allows personalised calculations.
- For high-mileage drivers (15,000–20,000 miles/yr) the annual savings are significantly higher.
- For drivers without home charging (public only), savings are reduced significantly or may be negative.
